problem: Let $I=[0,1]⊂R$ and ${X}_{i}={i}\times [0,{i}^{3}].$ Which of the following represents ${⋃}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}?$

feedback.problem: Which of the following is a representation of the set $S=R\times R$ in the Cartesian plane?
feedback.worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

$$
A\times B={(a,b)\,:\,a\in A,\,b\in B}
$$

In this case, the set

$$
S=R\times R
$$

contains every point in ${R}^{2}$ whose $x$-coordinate is any real number and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number.

$$
S={(x,y)\,:\,x\in R,\,y\in R}.
$$

To visualize $S$, consider ${S}_{0}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $0$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number.

$$
{S}_{0}={(0,y)\,:\,y\in R}
$$

We can represent ${S}_{0}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/07a3d9a6c38b5bfcc529496735a1a66eaceefd5ae3437a2cb0cd45911eccafae.png)

Now, consider a general ${S}_{i}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals some $i\in R$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number.

$$
{S}_{i}={(i,y)\,:\,y\in R}
$$

For each $i\in R,$ ${S}_{i}$ is a vertical line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/e454f1cf125486ca25acf15e26efd251a4a03b08e899814ab3e77db7898713c4.png)

Our Cartesian product $S$ is the union of these subsets over $R:$

$$
S={⋃}_{i\in R}{S}_{i}.
$$

This is the whole plane, as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/070389fcdb6d69f9aa90dabbd98a0d3461e26d3e3e08b1d53b92e99688c09923.png)
